transcript:
Header: 2026-07-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (CTO, NovaDocs), Marta Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Kim (DevOps)

Summary: Demo focused on migration parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API; discussed endpoints, function calling, streaming, model variants, cost/latency tradeoffs, private deployment options and security. Agreed next steps: share parity doc, run benchmarks, send security pack, schedule follow-up.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to walk through what a migration from openai/anthropic/together looks like to the redwood api, priya will jump into the console and the api parity mapping
00:18 Priya: hi all, quick agenda, 1) parity mapping—endpoints + params, 2) console + optimize for cost, 3) deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and 4) Q&A and next steps
00:35 Sam: sounds good, our main goals are reduce token cost and keep latency similar; also need vpc support for regulated docs, we've got SOC2 and some EU residency requests
00:50 Marta: and parity on function calling is critical, we use openai function calling heavily and anthropic tool calls for our internal agent workflows
01:05 Priya: yep, we mapped all three - openai/anthropic/together - to redwood equivalents. for example: OpenAI chat completions -> /v1/chat.generate (Redwood) with messages param, streaming via server-sent events; function-calling maps to Redwood's structured tool calls (the JSON schema support is same-ish but small differences in naming)
01:30 Jordan: quick q, what about streaming tokens and chunk sizes, we do streaming for typing indicators in product
01:40 Priya: Redwood supports SSE streaming and websocket in dedicated; chunk sizes are configurable, and batching won't block streaming for real-time paths, there's a lower-latency mode, but if you enable heavy batching you'll trade throughput for a bit of latency
01:58 Alex: we also recommend prefix/KV caching for repeated context to drop token usage, it's part of Redwood Optimize suggestions
02:15 Marta: how about model names — we call text-davinci-003 and Claude-instant in our scripts, how does that map
02:25 Priya: we expose a model catalog and also aliasing — you can map your existing model name to a Redwood model alias. e.g. text-davinci-003 -> rwd-gptx-13b-compat, claude-instant -> rwd-claude-sim-2. the compatibility profiles show differences in tokens/best-practices
02:45 Sam: any gotchas for prompt templates? we templatize heavily and use role / system messages differently between vendors
02:55 Priya: typically you only need to translate a few fields — system vs assistant naming — the SDK has a small shim to convert OpenAI payloads. for anthropic we handle the "assistant"/"assistant_prompt" differences with a helper in our SDKs, but you may need to adjust temperature/penalties slightly for parity
03:20 Jordan: network setup: if we want VPC, is it private control plane or fully customer managed? we can't send unredacted docs out of our subnet
03:32 Alex: for private deployments we support VPC and an on-prem package; there's an option for a customer-managed control plane for air-gapped needs. we'll send the network diagram and KMS integration notes
03:50 Marta: what about audit logs and retention? compliance team cares
03:58 Alex: audit logs, per-request metadata, and token-level tracing are available; retention tiers are an add-on, but SOC2 reports and logs export are standard for enterprise plans
04:15 Priya: demo time — I'll share my screen, first the console. you can see model catalog, route-level cost estimates, and optimize suggestions like quantization or batching flags per route
04:35 Priya: (screen) here is the parity mapping doc link in console, note the right panel shows differences for function call fields and an automated shim you can toggle per route
05:00 Marta: i see "auto-shim" — does it change output format? our downstream parsers expect strict JSON
05:10 Priya: the shim preserves output schema, it only translates request-side fields; if you want strict enforcement we have a structured-output plugin you can enable that validates JSON schemas and will fail requests that don't match
05:30 Sam: ok can you show an example migration snippet from OpenAI to Redwood?
05:38 Priya: sure, here's a curl for OpenAI and the Redwood equivalent, it's mostly one-to-one: messages -> messages, model param -> model alias, and function call object maps to tools schema. also streaming example with SSE header
06:05 Priya: (reads code) note rate limit headers are slightly different, Redwood returns x-rw-rlimit and a quota id; we also provide per-route quotas so you can mimic OpenAI's per-key behavior
06:30 Jordan: curious about throughput — our batch jobs use Together's batching for embedding/rerank, will Redwood support that scale on dedicated?
06:40 Priya: yes dedicated supports high-throughput pools, autoscaling policies, and burst capacity. for embeddings we have continuous batching optimizations and GPU-friendly kernels; we'll share a performance profile that shows throughput vs latency for 8k batch sizes
07:05 Alex: a typical migration path we recommend: 1) parity shim in SDK + aliasing, 2) run smoke tests in hosted, 3) run benchmarks on Dedicated if you need throughput guarantees, 4) move to private if you need VPC/KMS.
07:30 Sam: cost question — roughly how much savings can we expect vs OpenAI?
07:39 Priya: depends on models and quantization; we often see 20-50% token cost reduction using batching + quantization profiles on similar-quality open models. we'll put numbers in the parity doc for your actual token mix
07:55 Marta: can Redwood do canary rollouts with fallback to OpenAI if something breaks?
08:03 Alex: yes you can do route-level rollouts and automatic fallback to a secondary provider; it's a first-class policy in the console
08:20 Jordan: security — KMS? HSM? SSO?
08:26 Alex: KMS integrations supported, HSM via Private deployments, SSO/SAML with SCIM and role-based access controls are supported. we'll attach our security pack and an instance of SOC2 report
08:40 Priya: quick demo of Optimize: it suggests per-route batching, cache TTL, and pick quantization profiles based on seq length distribution. here's a sample suggestion for your reranker route to drop tokens 30%
09:05 Marta: we'll need to audit that suggestion against our quality tests — can't drop without validation
09:11 Priya: totally, Optimize ties to evals and you can run A/B tests with rollback on quality regressions
09:25 Sam: ok show me the API parity for function calling one more time
09:30 Priya: (walks through) Anthropics tool calls map to Redwood tools. small difference is anthropic sometimes uses different meta fields; we keep a translator and also let you supply a tools-schema mapping file
09:55 Sam: and error handling? we need idempotency and retry headers for background jobs
10:03 Priya: Redwood returns request-id, edge-ttl and retry-after headers similar to others; for idempotency you can pass idempotency-key header and we will dedupe depending on route config
10:20 Jordan: what about on-prem install footprint? GPU requirements and infra diagrams please
10:28 Alex: for on-prem we support multi-node with N GPUs per node, recommended 8xA100 for heavy throughput but smaller footprints for inference-only. we'll send the install guide and infra recommendations
10:45 Marta: latency SLO, we need p95 under 120ms for chat under 2k tokens
10:52 Priya: on hosted we can get close depending on model size; dedicated with optimized kernels will meet p95 120ms for 2k tokens for rwd-gptx-13b-compat, we'll include benchmark results
11:10 Sam: any hidden migration cost like refactoring prompts across templates?
11:18 Priya: usually minor: prompt templates sometimes need small translation, and some hyperparam tuning. our SDK shim reduces effort but plan a couple sprints for full parity testing
11:35 Jordan: ok for compliance, can we host logs in our S3 and have control over retention?
11:43 Alex: yes logs export to customer-controlled S3 with encryption via your KMS; retention configurable per account
11:55 Priya: last part of demo — the console shows a migration helper that will generate a mapping bundle (aliases, shims, route configs) you can download and apply. you can also run a dry-run that proxies traffic to both providers and compares outputs
12:20 Sam: dry-run/proxy sounds useful, can it do A/B with weighted traffic?
12:28 Priya: yes, you can set weights and automatic divergence alerts if response quality falls below threshold
12:40 Marta: who should we send security questions to?
12:45 Alex: send them to security@redwood.ai and cc me, we'll have our security engineer circle back; Jordan can also get the network diagram
12:55 Sam: recap — parity doc + pricing, perf benchmarks, security pack, dry-run setup; sounds good
13:10 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc. any final q?
13:17 Marta: nope, thanks
13:20 Jordan: thanks all
13:22 Alex: bye

End of transcript
